13         40.4 Device Translating Callbacks
14         Summary
15         A tool provides device-translating callbacks, which have the device-translating property, to perform
16         any necessary translations between devices on which the tool and OMPD library run and on which
17         the OpenMP program runs.

18         40.4.1 OMPD device_host Type
            Name: device_host                                        Properties: C-only, OMPD
19
            Category: function pointer
20         Return Type and Arguments
            Name                                       Type                         Properties
            <return type>                              rc                           default
            address_space_context                      address_space_context        pointer
21          input                                      void                         intent(in), pointer
            unit_size                                  size                         default
            count                                      size                         default
            output                                     void                         pointer
22         Type Signature
                                                           C
23          typedef ompd_rc_t (*ompd_callback_device_host_fn_t) (
24            ompd_address_space_context_t *address_space_context,
25            const void *input, ompd_size_t unit_size, ompd_size_t count,
26            void *output);
                                                           C

     842   OpenMP API – Version 6.0 November 2024
 1   Semantics
 2   The architecture on which the third-party tool and the OMPD library execute may be different from
 3   the architecture on which the OpenMP program that is being examined executes. Thus, the
 4   conventions for representing data may differ. The callback interface includes operations to convert
 5   between the conventions, such as the byte order (endianness), that the tool and OMPD library use
 6   and the ones that the OpenMP program uses. The device_host OMPD type is the type
 7   signature of the device_to_host and host_to_device callbacks that the tool provides to
 8   convert data between formats.
 9   The address_space_context argument specifies the address space that is associated with the data.
10   The input argument is the source buffer and the output argument is the destination buffer. The
11   unit_size argument is the size of each of the elements to be converted. The count argument is the
12   number of elements to be transformed.
13   The OMPD library allocates and owns the input and output buffers. It must ensure that the buffers
14   have the correct size and are eventually deallocated when they are no longer needed.
15   Cross References

     844   OpenMP API – Version 6.0 November 2024
 1   41 OMPD Routines
 2   This chapter defines the OMPD routines, which are routines that have the OMPD property and,
 3   thus, are provided by the OMPD library to be used by third-party tools. Some OMPD routines
 4   require one or more specified threads to be stopped for the returned values to be meaningful. In this
 5   context, a stopped thread is a thread that is not modifying the observable OpenMP runtime state.


 6   41.1 OMPD Library Initialization and Finalization
 7   The OMPD library must be initialized exactly once after it is loaded, and finalized exactly once
 8   before it is unloaded. Per OpenMP process or core file initialization and finalization are also
 9   required. Once loaded, the tool can determine the version of the OMPD API that the library
10   supports by calling ompd_get_api_version. If the tool supports the version that
11   ompd_get_api_version returns, the tool starts the initialization by calling
12   ompd_initialize using the version of the OMPD API that the library supports. If the tool
13   does not support the version that ompd_get_api_version returns, it may attempt to call
14   ompd_initialize with a different version.

15   Cross References
16      • ompd_get_api_version Routine, see Section 41.1.2
17      • ompd_initialize Routine, see Section 41.1.1


18   41.1.1 ompd_initialize Routine
      Name: ompd_initialize                                    Properties: C-only, OMPD
19
      Category: function
20   Return Type and Arguments
      Name                                        Type                        Properties
      <return type>                               rc                          default
21
      api_version                                 word                        default
      callbacks                                   callbacks                   intent(in), pointer

22   Prototypes
                                                     C
23   ompd_rc_t ompd_initialize(ompd_word_t api_version,
24     const ompd_callbacks_t *callbacks);
                                                     C


                                                           CHAPTER 41. OMPD ROUTINES                    845
 1         Semantics
 2         A tool that uses OMPD calls ompd_initialize to initialize each OMPD library that it loads.
 3         More than one library may be present in a third-party tool because the tool may control multiple
 4         devices, which may use different runtime systems that require different OMPD libraries. This
 5         initialization must be performed exactly once before the tool can begin to operate on an OpenMP
 6         process or core file.
 7         The api_version argument is the OMPD API version that the tool requests to use. The tool may call
 8         ompd_get_api_version to obtain the latest OMPD API version that the OMPD library
 9         supports.
10         The tool provides the OMPD library with a set of callbacks in the callbacks input argument, which
11         enables the OMPD library to allocate and to deallocate memory in the address space of the tool, to
12         lookup the sizes of basic primitive types in the device, to lookup symbols in the device, and to read
13         and to write memory in the device.
14         This routine returns ompd_rc_bad_input if invalid callbacks are provided. In addition to the
15         return codes permitted for all OMPD routines, this routine may return ompd_rc_unsupported
16         if the requested API version cannot be provided.

 9   41.1.3 ompd_get_version_string Routine
      Name: ompd_get_version_string                             Properties: C-only, OMPD
10
      Category: function
11   Return Type and Arguments
      Name                                        Type                          Properties
      <return type>                               rc                            default
12
      string                                      const char                    intent(out), pointer-to-
                                                                                pointer

13   Prototypes
                                                      C
14    ompd_rc_t ompd_get_version_string(const char **string);
                                                      C
15   Semantics
16   The ompd_get_version_string routine returns a pointer to a descriptive version string of
17   the OMPD library vendor, implementation, internal version, date, or any other information that may
18   be useful to a tool user or vendor. An implementation should provide a different string for every
19   change to its source code or build that could be visible to the OMPD user.
20   A pointer to a descriptive version string is placed into the location to which the string output
21   argument points. The OMPD library owns the string that the OMPD library returns; the tool must
22   not modify or release this string. The string remains valid for as long as the library is loaded. The
23   ompd_get_version_string routine may be called before ompd_initialize.
24   Accordingly, the OMPD library must not use heap or stack memory for the string.
25   The signatures of ompd_get_api_version and ompd_get_version_string are
26   guaranteed not to change in future versions of OMPD. In contrast, the type definitions and
27   prototypes in the rest of OMPD do not carry the same guarantee. Therefore a tool that uses OMPD
28   should check the version of the loaded OMPD library before it calls any other OMPD routine.

 5         41.1.4 ompd_finalize Routine
            Name: ompd_finalize                                      Properties: C-only, OMPD
 6
            Category: function

 7         Return Type
            Name                                       Type                         Properties
 8
            <return type>                              rc                           default

 9         Prototypes
                                                           C
10          ompd_rc_t ompd_finalize(void);
                                                           C
11         Semantics
12         When the tool is finished with the OMPD library, it should call ompd_finalize before it
13         unloads the library. The call to the ompd_finalize routine must be the last OMPD call that the
14         tool makes before it unloads the library. This routine allows the OMPD library to free any resources
15         that it may be holding. The OMPD library may implement a finalizer section, which executes as the
16         library is unloaded and therefore after the call to ompd_finalize. During finalization, the
17         OMPD library may use the callbacks that the tool provided earlier during the call to
18         ompd_initialize. In addition to the return codes permitted for all OMPD routines, this
19         routine returns ompd_rc_unsupported if the OMPD library is not initialized.

20         Cross References
21            • OMPD rc Type, see Section 39.9

12   41.7 Handle Comparing Routines
13   This section describes handle-comparing routines, which are routines that have the
14   handle-comparing property and, thus, enable the comparison of two handles. The internal structure
15   of handles is opaque to tools. While tools can easily compare pointers to handles, they cannot
16   determine whether handles at two different addresses refer to the same underlying context and
17   instead must use a handle-comparing routine.
18   On success, a handle-comparing routine returns, in the location to which its cmp_value argument
19   points, a signed integer value that indicates how the underlying contexts compare. A value less than,
20   equal to, or greater than 0 indicates that the context to which <handle-type>_handle_1 corresponds
21   is, respectively, less than, equal to, or greater than that to which <handle-type>_handle_2
22   corresponds. The <handle-type>_handle_1 and <handle-type>_handle_2 arguments are handles
23   that correspond to the type of handle that the routine compares. In each handle-comparing routine,
24   <handle-type> is replaced with the name of the type of handle that the routine compares. For all
25   types of handles, the means by which two handles are ordered is implementation defined.

16   41.8 Handle Releasing Routines
17   This section describes handle-releasing routines, which are routines that have the handle-releasing
18   property and, thus, release a handle owned by a tool. When a tool finishes with a handle that a
19   handle argument identifies, it should release it with the corresponding handle-releasing routine so
20   the OMPD library can release any resources that it has related to the corresponding context.

21   Restrictions
22   Restrictions to handle-releasing routines are as follows:
23      • A context must not be used after its corresponding handle is released.

22   41.9 Querying Thread States
23   41.9.1 ompd_enumerate_states Routine
      Name: ompd_enumerate_states                         Properties: C-only, OMPD
24
      Category: function



                                                    CHAPTER 41. OMPD ROUTINES                 869
1          Return Type and Arguments
            Name                                        Type                         Properties
            <return type>                               rc                           default
            address_space_handle                        address_space_handle         opaque, pointer
            current_state                               word                         default
2
            next_state                                  word                         pointer
            next_state_name                             const char                   intent(out), pointer-to-
                                                                                     pointer
            more_enums                                  word                         pointer

3          Prototypes
                                                            C
4           ompd_rc_t ompd_enumerate_states(
5             ompd_address_space_handle_t *address_space_handle,
6             ompd_word_t current_state, ompd_word_t *next_state,
7             const char **next_state_name, ompd_word_t *more_enums);
                                                            C
 8         Semantics
 9         An OpenMP implementation may support only a subset of the states that the state OMPT type
10         defines. In addition, an OpenMP implementation may support implementation defined states. The
11         ompd_enumerate_states routine enumerates the thread states that an OpenMP
12         implementation supports.
13         When the current_state argument is a thread state that an OpenMP implementation supports, the
14         routine assigns the value and string name of the next thread state in the enumeration to the locations
15         to which the next_state and next_state_name arguments point. On return, the tool owns the
16         next_state_name string. The OMPD library allocates storage for the string with the
17         alloc_memory callback that the tool provides. The tool is responsible for releasing the storage.
18         On return, the location to which the more_enums argument points has the value 1 whenever one or
19         more states are left in the enumeration. On return, the location to which the more_enums argument
20         points has the value 0 when current_state is the last state in the enumeration.
21         The address_space_handle argument identifies the address space. The current_state argument must
22         be a thread state that the OpenMP implementation supports. To begin enumerating the supported
23         states, a tool should pass ompt_state_undefined as the value of current_state. Subsequent
24         calls to ompd_enumerate_states by the tool should pass the value that the routine returned in
25         the next_state argument. This routine returns ompd_rc_bad_input if an unknown value is
26         provided in current_state.

 1   Cross References
 2      • OMPD address_space_handle Type, see Section 39.18.1
 3      • OMPD rc Type, see Section 39.9
 4      • OMPT state Type, see Section 33.31

 1         41.10 Display Control Variables
 2         41.10.1 ompd_get_display_control_vars Routine
            Name: ompd_get_display_control_vars                     Properties: C-only, OMPD
 3
            Category: function
 4         Return Type and Arguments
            Name                                      Type                        Properties
            <return type>                             rc                          default
 5
            address_space_handle                      address_space_handle        opaque, pointer
            control_vars                              const char * const *        intent(out), pointer

 6         Prototypes
                                                          C
 7          ompd_rc_t ompd_get_display_control_vars(
 8            ompd_address_space_handle_t *address_space_handle,
 9            const char * const * *control_vars);
                                                          C
10         Semantics
11         The ompd_get_display_control_vars routine returns a list of OpenMP control variables
12         as a NULL-terminated vector of null-terminated strings of name/value pairs. These control
13         variables have user-controllable settings and are important to the operation or performance of an
14         OpenMP runtime system. The control variables that this interface exposes include all OpenMP
15         environment variables, settings that may come from vendor or platform-specific environment
16         variables, and other settings that affect the operation or functioning of an OpenMP runtime. The
17         format of the strings is NAME ’=’ VALUE. NAME corresponds to the control variable name,
18         optionally prepended with a bracketed DEVICE. VALUE corresponds to the value of the control
19         variable.
20         On return, the tool owns the vector and the strings. The OMPD library must satisfy the termination
21         constraints; it may use static or dynamic memory for the vector and/or the strings and is
22         unconstrained in how it arranges them in memory. If it uses dynamic memory then the OMPD
23         library must use the alloc_memory callback that the tool provides. The tool must use the
24         ompd_rel_display_control_vars routine to release the vector and the strings.
25         The address_space_handle argument identifies the address space. On return, the control_vars
26         argument points to the vector of display control variables.

16   41.11.1 ompd_enumerate_icvs Routine
      Name: ompd_enumerate_icvs                           Properties: C-only, OMPD
17
      Category: function
18   Return Type and Arguments
      Name                                   Type                     Properties
      <return type>                          rc                       default
      handle                                 address_space_handle     opaque, pointer
      current                                icv_id                   default
19    next_id                                icv_id                   pointer
      next_icv_name                          const char               intent(out), pointer-to-
                                                                      pointer
      next_scope                             scope                    pointer
      more                                   integer                  pointer




                                                       CHAPTER 41. OMPD ROUTINES                 873
1          Prototypes
                                                          C
2           ompd_rc_t ompd_enumerate_icvs(
3             ompd_address_space_handle_t *handle, ompd_icv_id_t current,
4             ompd_icv_id_t *next_id, const char **next_icv_name,
5             ompd_scope_t *next_scope, int *more);
                                                          C
 6         Semantics
 7         The ompd_enumerate_icvs routine enables a tool to enumerate the ICVs that an OpenMP
 8         implementation supports and their related scopes. An OpenMP implementation must support all
 9         ICVs listed in Section 3.1. An OpenMP implementation may support additional implementation
10         defined ICVs. An implementation may store ICVs in a different scope than Section 3.1 indicates.
11         When the current argument is set to the identifier of a supported ICV, ompd_enumerate_icvs
12         assigns the value, string name, and scope of the next ICV in the enumeration to the locations to
13         which the next_id, next_icv_name, and next_scope arguments point. On return, the tool owns the
14         next_icv_name string. The OMPD library uses the alloc_memory callback that the tool provides
15         to allocate the string storage; the tool is responsible for releasing the memory.
16         On return, the location to which the more argument points has the value of 1 whenever one or more
17         ICVs are left in the enumeration. On return, that location has the value 0 when current is the last
18         ICV in the enumeration. The address_space_handle argument identifies the address space. The
19         current argument must be an ICV that the OpenMP implementation supports. To begin
20         enumerating the ICVs, a tool should pass ompd_icv_undefined as the value of current.
21         Subsequent calls to ompd_enumerate_icvs should pass the value returned by the routine in the
22         next_id output argument. On return, the next_id argument points to an integer with the value of the
23         ID of the next ICV in the enumeration. On return, the next_icv_name argument points to a character
24         string with the name of the next ICV. On return, the value to which the next_scope argument points
25         identifies the scope of the next ICV. On return, the more_enums argument points to an integer with
26         the value of 1 when more ICVs are left to enumerate and the value of 0 when no more ICVs are
27         left. This routine returns ompd_rc_bad_input if an unknown value is provided in current.

28         Cross References

                                                          CHAPTER 41. OMPD ROUTINES                877
 1         42 OMPD Breakpoint Symbol Names
 2         The OpenMP implementation must define several symbols through which execution must pass
 3         when particular events occur and data collection for OMPD is enabled. A third-party tool can
 4         enable notification of an event by setting a breakpoint at the address of the symbol.
 5         OMPD symbols have external C linkage and do not require demangling or other transformations to
 6         look up their names to obtain the address in the OpenMP program. While each OMPD symbol
 7         conceptually has a function type signature, it may not be a function. It may be a labeled location.

 8         42.1 ompd_bp_thread_begin Breakpoint
 9         Format
                                                           C
10          void ompd_bp_thread_begin(void);
                                                           C
11         Semantics
12         When starting a native thread that will be used as an OpenMP thread, the implementation must
13         execute ompd_bp_thread_begin. Thus, the OpenMP implementation must execute
14         ompd_bp_thread_begin at every native-thread-begin and initial-thread-begin event. This
15         execution occurs before the thread starts the execution of any OpenMP region.

16         42.2 ompd_bp_thread_end Breakpoint
17         Format
                                                           C
18          void ompd_bp_thread_end(void);
                                                           C
19         Semantics
20         When terminating an OpenMP thread or a native thread that has been used as an OpenMP thread,
21         the implementation must execute ompd_bp_thread_end. Thus, the OpenMP implementation
22         must execute ompd_bp_thread_end at every native-thread-end and initial-thread-end event.
23         This execution occurs after the thread completes the execution of all OpenMP regions. After
24         executing ompd_bp_thread_end, any thread_handle that was acquired for this thread is invalid
25         and should be released by calling ompd_rel_thread_handle.

26         Cross References
27            • ompd_rel_thread_handle Routine, see Section 41.8.4



     878   OpenMP API – Version 6.0 November 2024
 1   42.3 ompd_bp_device_begin Breakpoint
 2   Format
                                                     C
 3   void ompd_bp_device_begin(void);
                                                     C
 4   Semantics
 5   When initializing a device for execution of target regions, the implementation must execute
 6   ompd_bp_device_begin. Thus, the OpenMP implementation must execute
 7   ompd_bp_device_begin at every device-initialize event. This execution occurs before the
 8   work associated with any OpenMP region executes on the device.
 9   Cross References
10      • Device Initialization, see Section 15.4
11      • target Construct, see Section 15.8

12   42.4 ompd_bp_device_end Breakpoint
13   Format
                                                     C
14   void ompd_bp_device_end(void);
                                                     C
15   Semantics
16   When terminating use of a device, the implementation must execute ompd_bp_device_end.
17   Thus, the OpenMP implementation must execute ompd_bp_device_end at every
18   device-finalize event. This execution occurs after the device executes all OpenMP regions. After
19   execution of ompd_bp_device_end, any address_space_handle that was acquired for this
20   device is invalid and should be released by calling ompd_rel_address_space_handle.
21   Cross References
22      • Device Initialization, see Section 15.4
23      • ompd_rel_address_space_handle Routine, see Section 41.8.1


24   42.5 ompd_bp_parallel_begin Breakpoint
25   Format
                                                     C
26   void ompd_bp_parallel_begin(void);
                                                     C



                                  CHAPTER 42. OMPD BREAKPOINT SYMBOL NAMES                          879
 1         Semantics
 2         Before starting execution of a parallel region, the implementation must execute
 3         ompd_bp_parallel_begin. Thus, the OpenMP implementation must execute
 4         ompd_bp_parallel_begin at every parallel-begin event. When the implementation reaches
 5         ompd_bp_parallel_begin, the binding region for
 6         ompd_get_curr_parallel_handle is the parallel region that is beginning and the

 1         42.9 ompd_bp_task_begin Breakpoint
 2         Format
                                                          C
 3          void ompd_bp_task_begin(void);
                                                          C
 4         Semantics
 5         Before starting execution of a task region, the implementation must execute
 6         ompd_bp_task_begin. Thus, the OpenMP implementation must execute

                                                          C

17         ompd_bp_task_end. Thus, the OpenMP implementation must execute ompd_bp_task_end
18         immediately after completion of a structured block that is associated with a non-merged task. When
19         the implementation reaches ompd_bp_task_end, the binding task set for
20         ompd_get_curr_task_handle is the task that finished execution. After execution of
21         ompd_bp_task_end, any task_handle that was acquired for the task region is invalid and should
22         be released by calling ompd_rel_task_handle.

    884   OpenMP API – Version 6.0 November 2024
1    A OpenMP Implementation-Defined
2      Behaviors
3    This appendix summarizes the behaviors that are described as implementation defined in the
4    OpenMP API. Each behavior is cross-referenced back to its description in the main specification.
5    An implementation is required to define and to document its behavior in these cases.

6    Chapter 1:
 7      • Memory model: The minimum size at which a memory update may also read and write back
 8        adjacent variables that are part of an aggregate variable is implementation defined but is no
 9        larger than the base language requires. The manner in which a program can obtain the
10        referenced device address from a device pointer, outside the mechanisms specified by
11        OpenMP, is implementation defined (see Section 1.3.1).
12      • Device data environments: Whether a variable with static storage duration that is accessible
13        on a device and is not a device-local variable is mapped with a persistent self map at the
14        beginning of the program is implementation defined (see Section 1.3.2).

15   Chapter 2:
16      • Processor: A hardware unit that is implementation defined (see Chapter 2).
17      • Device: An implementation defined logical execution engine (see Chapter 2).
18      • Device pointer: An implementation defined handle that refers to a device address (see
19        Chapter 2).
20      • Supported active levels of parallelism: The maximum number of active parallel regions
21        that may enclose any region of code in an OpenMP program is implementation defined (see
22        Chapter 2).
23      • Deprecated features: For any deprecated feature, whether any modifications provided by its
24        replacement feature (if any) apply to the deprecated feature is implementation defined (see
25        Chapter 2).

26   Chapter 3:
27     • Internal control variables: The initial values of dyn-var, nthreads-var, run-sched-var,
28       bind-var, stacksize-var, wait-policy-var, thread-limit-var, max-active-levels-var,
29       place-partition-var, affinity-format-var, default-device-var, num-procs-var and
30       def-allocator-var are implementation defined (see Section 3.2).




                   APPENDIX A. OPENMP IMPLEMENTATION-DEFINED BEHAVIORS                             885
1          Chapter 4:
2             • OMP_DYNAMIC environment variable: If the value is neither true nor false, the
3               behavior of the program is implementation defined (see Section 4.1.2).
4             • OMP_NUM_THREADS environment variable: If any value of the specified list leads to a
5               number of threads that is greater than the implementation can support, or if any value is not a
6               positive integer, then the behavior of the program is implementation defined (see
7               Section 4.1.3).
 8            • OMP_THREAD_LIMIT environment variable: If the requested value is greater than the
 9              number of threads that an implementation can support, or if the value is not a positive integer,
10              the behavior of the program is implementation defined (see Section 4.1.4).
11            • OMP_MAX_ACTIVE_LEVELS environment variable: If the value is a negative integer or is
12              greater than the maximum number of nested active levels that an implementation can support
13              then the behavior of the program is implementation defined (see Section 4.1.5).
14            • OMP_PLACES environment variable: The meaning of the numbers specified in the
15              environment variable and how the numbering is done are implementation defined. The
16              precise definitions of the abstract names are implementation defined. An implementation
17              may add implementation defined abstract names as appropriate for the target platform. When
18              creating a place list of n elements by appending the number n to an abstract name, the
19              determination of which resources to include in the place list is implementation defined. When
20              requesting more resources than available, the length of the place list is also implementation
21              defined. The behavior of the program is implementation defined when the execution
22              environment cannot map a numerical value (either explicitly defined or implicitly derived
23              from an interval) within the OMP_PLACES list to a processor on the target platform, or if it
24              maps to an unavailable processor. The behavior is also implementation defined when the
25              OMP_PLACES environment variable is defined using an abstract name (see Section 4.1.6).
26            • OMP_PROC_BIND environment variable: If the value is not true, false, or a comma
27              separated list of primary, close, or spread, the behavior is implementation defined.
28              The behavior is also implementation defined if an initial thread cannot be bound to the first
29              place in the OpenMP place list. The thread affinity policy is implementation defined if the
30              value is true (see Section 4.1.7).
31            • OMP_SCHEDULE environment variable: If the value does not conform to the specified
32              format then the behavior of the program is implementation defined (see Section 4.3.1).
33            • OMP_STACKSIZE environment variable: If the value does not conform to the specified
34              format or the implementation cannot provide a stack of the specified size then the behavior is
35              implementation defined (see Section 4.3.2).
36            • OMP_WAIT_POLICY environment variable: The details of the active and passive
37              behaviors are implementation defined (see Section 4.3.3).
38            • OMP_DISPLAY_AFFINITY environment variable: For all values of the environment
39              variable other than true or false, the display action is implementation defined (see
40              Section 4.3.4).



     886   OpenMP API – Version 6.0 November 2024
 1      • OMP_AFFINITY_FORMAT environment variable: Additional implementation defined
 2        field types can be added (see Section 4.3.5).
 3      • OMP_CANCELLATION environment variable: If the value is set to neither true nor
 4        false, the behavior of the program is implementation defined (see Section 4.3.6).
 5      • OMP_TARGET_OFFLOAD environment variable: The support of disabled is
 6        implementation defined (see Section 4.3.9).
 7      • OMP_THREADS_RESERVE environment variable: If the requested values are greater than
 8        OMP_THREAD_LIMIT, the behavior of the program is implementation defined (see
 9        Section 4.3.10).
10      • OMP_TOOL_LIBRARIES environment variable: Whether the value of the environment
11        variable is case sensitive is implementation defined (see Section 4.5.2).
12      • OMP_TOOL_VERBOSE_INIT environment variable: Support for logging to stdout or
13        stderr is implementation defined. Whether the value of the environment variable is case
14        sensitive when it is treated as a filename is implementation defined. The format and detail of
15        the log is implementation defined (see Section 4.5.3).
16      • OMP_DEBUG environment variable: If the value is neither disabled nor enabled, the
17        behavior is implementation defined (see Section 4.6.1).
18      • OMP_NUM_TEAMS environment variable: If the value is not a positive integer or is greater
19        than the number of teams that an implementation can support, the behavior of the program is
20        implementation defined (see Section 4.2.1).
21      • OMP_TEAMS_THREAD_LIMIT environment variable: If the value is not a positive integer
22        or is greater than the number of threads that an implementation can support, the behavior of
23        the program is implementation defined (see Section 4.2.2).

 1         B Features History
 2         This appendix summarizes the major changes between OpenMP API versions since version 2.5.

 3         B.1 Deprecated Features
 4         The following features were deprecated in Version 6.0:
                                                      Fortran
 5            • Omitting the optional white space to separate adjacent keywords in the directive-name in free
 6              source form and fixed source form directives is deprecated (see Section 5.1.1 and
 7              Section 5.1.2).
                                                      Fortran
 8            • The syntax of the declare_reduction directive that specifies the combiner expression
 9              in the directive argument was deprecated (see Section 7.6.14).
10            • The Fortran include file omp_lib.h has been deprecated (see Chapter 20).
11            • The target, target_data_op, target_submit and target_map values of the
12              callbacks OMPT types and the associated trace record OMPT type names were
13              deprecated (see Section 33.6).
14            • The ompt_target_data_transfer_to_device,
15              ompt_target_data_transfer_from_device,
16              ompt_target_data_transfer_to_device_async, and
17              ompt_target_data_transfer_from_device_async values in the
18              target_data_op OMPT type were deprecated (see Section 33.35).
19            • The target_data_op, target, target_map and target_submit callbacks and
20              the associated trace record OMPT type names were deprecated (see Section 35.7,
21              Section 35.8, Section 35.9 and Section 35.10).

22         B.2 Version 5.2 to 6.0 Differences
23            • All features deprecated in versions 5.0, 5.1 and 5.2 were removed.
24            • Full support for C23, C++23, and Fortran 2023 was added (see Section 1.6).
25            • Full support of Fortran 2018 was completed (see Section 1.6).
26            • The environment variable syntax was extended to support initializing ICVs for the host device
27              and non-host devices with a single environment variable (see Section 3.2 and Chapter 4).




     896   OpenMP API – Version 6.0 November 2024
 1   • The handling of the nthreads-var ICV was updated (see Section 3.4) and the nthreads
 2     argument of the num_threads clause was changed to a list (see Section 12.1.2) to support
 3     context-specific reservation of inner parallelism.
 4   • Numeric abstract name values are now allowed for the OMP_NUM_THREADS,
 5     OMP_THREAD_LIMIT and OMP_TEAMS_THREAD_LIMIT environment variables (see
 6     Section 4.1.3, Section 4.1.4 and Section 4.2.2).
 7   • The environment variable OMP_PLACES was extended to support an increment between
 8     consecutive places when creating a place list from an abstract name (see Section 4.1.6).
 9   • The environment variable OMP_AVAILABLE_DEVICES was added and the environment
10     variable OMP_DEFAULT_DEVICE was extended to support device selection by traits (see
11     Section 4.3.7 and Section 4.3.8).
12   • The uid trait was added to the permissible traits in the environment variables
13     OMP_AVAILABLE_DEVICES and OMP_DEFAULT_DEVICE and to the target device trait
14     set (see Section 4.3.7, Section 4.3.8 and Section 9.2).
15   • The environment variable OMP_THREADS_RESERVE was added to reserve a number of
16     structured threads and free-agent threads (see Section 4.3.10).
                                               C++
17   • The decl attribute was added to improve the attribute syntax for declarative directives (see
18     Section 5.1).
                                               C++
                                                C
19   • The OpenMP directive syntax was extended to include C attribute specifiers (see
20     Section 5.1).
                                               C
                                             Fortran
21   • Support for directives with the pure property in DO CONCURRENT constructs has been added
22     (see Section 5.1).
                                             Fortran
23   • To improve consistency in clause format, all inarguable clauses were extended to take an
24     optional argument for which the default value yields equivalent semantics to the existing
25     inarguable semantics (see Section 5.2).
26   • The adjust_args clause was extended to support positional specification of arguments
27     (see Section 5.2.1 and Section 9.6.2)
                                             Fortran
28   • The definitions of locator list items and assignable OpenMP types were extended to include
29     function references that have data pointer results (see Section 5.2.1).
                                             Fortran




                                                   APPENDIX B. FEATURES HISTORY                    897
                                                      C / C++
 1            • The array section definition was extended to permit, where explicitly allowed, omission of
 2              the length when the size of the array dimension is not known (see Section 5.2.5).
                                                      C / C++
 3            • To support greater specificity on compound constructs, all clauses were extended to accept
 4              the directive-name-modifier, which identifies the constituent directives to which the clause
 5              applies (see Section 5.4).
 6            • To allow specification of all modifiers of the init clause, extensions to the interop
 7              operation of the append_args clause were added (see Section 5.6 and Section 9.6.3).
 8            • The init clause was added to the depobj construct, and the construct now permits
 9              repeatable init, update, and destroy clauses (see Section 5.6 and Section 17.9.3).
10            • The syntax that omits the argument to the destroy clause for the depobj construct was
11              undeprecated (see Section 5.7).
                                                       Fortran
12            • Atomic structured blocks were extended to allow the BLOCK construct, pointer assignments
13              and two intrinsic functions for enum and enumeration types (see Section 6.3.3).
14            • conditional-update-statement was extended to allow more forms and comparisons (see
15              Section 6.3.3).
                                                       Fortran
16            • The concept of canonical loop sequences and the looprange clause were defined (see
17              Section 6.4.2 and Section 6.4.7).
                                                       Fortran
18            • For polymorphic types, restrictions were changed and behavior clarified for data-sharing
19              attribute clauses and data-mapping attribute clauses (see Chapter 7).
                                                       Fortran
20            • The saved modifier, the replayable clause, and the taskgraph construct were added to
21              support the recording and efficient replay execution of a sequence of task-generating
22              constructs (see Section 7.2, Section 14.6, and Section 14.3).
23            • The default clause is now allowed on the target directive, and, similarly to the
24              defaultmap clause, now accepts the variable-category modifier (see Section 7.5.1).
25            • The semantics of the use_device_ptr and use_device_addr clauses on a
26              target_data construct were altered to imply a reference count update on entry and exit
27              from the region for the corresponding objects that they reference in the device data
28              environment (see Section 7.5.8 and Section 7.5.10).
29            • Support for induction operations was added (see Section 7.6) through the induction
30              clause (see Section 7.6.13) and the declare_induction directive (see Section 7.6.17),
31              which supports user-defined induction.
32            • Support for reductions over private variables with the reduction clause has been added
33              (see Section 7.6).

                                               C++
 1   • The circumstances under which implicitly declared reduction identifiers are supported for

28   B.3 Version 5.1 to 5.2 Differences
29     • Major reorganization and numerous changes were made to improve the quality of the
30       specification of OpenMP syntax and to increase consistency of restrictions and their wording.
31       These changes frequently result in the possible perception of differences to preceding versions
32       of the OpenMP specification. However, those differences almost always resolve ambiguities,
33       which may nonetheless have implications for existing implementations and programs.
34     • The explicit-task-var ICV replaced the implicit-task-var ICV, with the opposite meaning and
35       semantics (see Chapter 3). The omp_in_explicit_task routine was added to query if a
36       code region is executed from an explicit task region (see Section 23.1.2).

     916   OpenMP API – Version 6.0 November 2024
1    C Nesting of Regions
2    This appendix describes a set of restrictions on the nesting of regions. The restrictions on nesting
3    are as follows:
4       • A teams region must be strictly nested either within the implicit parallel region that
5         surrounds the whole OpenMP program or within a target region. If a teams construct is
6         nested within a target construct, that target construct must contain no statements,
7         declarations or directives outside of the teams construct (see Section 12.2).
8       • Only regions that are generated by teams-nestable constructs or teams-nestable routines
9         may be strictly nested regions of teams regions (see Section 12.2).
10      • The only routines for which a call may be nested inside a region that corresponds to a
11        construct on which the order clause is specified with concurrent as the ordering
12        argument are order-concurrent-nestable routines (see Section 12.3).
13      • Only regions that correspond to order-concurrent-nestable constructs or
14        order-concurrent-nestable routines may be strictly nested regions of regions that
15        correspond to constructs on which the order clause is specified with concurrent as the
16        ordering argument (see Section 12.3).
17      • The only OpenMP constructs that can be encountered during execution of a simd region are
18        SIMDizable constructs (see Section 12.4).
19      • A team-executed region may not be closely nested inside a partitioned worksharing region, a
20        region that corresponds to a thread-exclusive construct, or a region that corresponds to a
21        task-generating construct that is not a team-generating construct. This follows from various
22        restrictions requiring, in general, that team-executed regions (which include worksharing
23        regions and barrier regions) are executed by all threads in a team or by none at all (see
24        Chapter 13 and Section 17.3.1).
25      • A distribute region must be strictly nested inside a teams region (see Section 13.7).
26      • A loop region that binds to a teams region must be strictly nested inside a teams region
27        (see Section 13.8.1).
28      • During execution of a target region, other than target constructs for which a device
29        clause on which the ancestor device-modifier appears, device-affecting constructs must not
30        be encountered (see Section 15.8).
31      • A critical region must not be nested (closely or otherwise) inside a critical region
32        with the same name (see Section 17.2).



                                                      APPENDIX C. NESTING OF REGIONS                   917
1             • OpenMP constructs may not be encountered during execution of an atomic region (see
2               Section 17.8.5).
3             • An ordered region that corresponds to an ordered construct with the threads or
4               doacross clause may not be closely nested inside a critical, ordered, loop, task,
5               or taskloop region (see Section 17.10).
6             • If the simd parallelization-level clause is specified on an ordered construct, the
7               ordered region must bind to a simd region or one that corresponds to a compound
8               construct for which the simd construct is a leaf construct (see Section 17.10.2).
 9            • If the threads parallelization-level clause is specified on an ordered construct, the
10              ordered region must bind to a worksharing-loop region or one that corresponds to a
11              compound construct for which a worksharing-loop construct is a leaf construct (see
12              Section 17.10.2).
13            • If the threads parallelization-level clause is specified on an ordered construct and the
14              binding region corresponds to a compound construct then the simd construct must not be a
15              leaf construct unless the simd parallelization-level clause is also specified (see
16              Section 17.10.2).
17            • If cancel-directive-name is taskgroup, the cancel construct must be closely nested
18              inside a task construct and the cancel region must be closely nested inside a
19              taskgroup region. Otherwise, the cancel construct must be closely nested inside a
20              construct for which directive-name is cancel-directive-name (see Section 18.2).
21            • A cancellation point construct for which cancel-directive-name is taskgroup
22              must be closely nested inside a task construct, and the cancellation point region
23              must be closely nested inside a taskgroup region. Otherwise, a cancellation
24              point construct must be closely nested inside a construct for which directive-name is
25              cancel-directive-name (see Section 18.3).
